# RealityCheck

RealityCheck is one progressive HTML workflow: check an export locally, repair a separate copy in Codex, then publish and prove the real HTTPS result. The zero-upload checker reads selected files only inside the user's browser. The no-clone Codex Skill path creates a bounded working copy, makes justified repairs, reruns the same detector, and returns the before technical report, repaired working copy, after report, and detected unresolved decisions. It calls the copy directly usable only when the after verification meets the Skill delivery gate. Publish mode freezes exact passive-static bytes; live verification binds an authorized deployment back to the same capsule.

For professional Web QA, RealityCheck can preview a bilingual audit plan before browser access. It then uses a real installed Chrome, Edge, or Chromium browser to stress responsive layouts, user journeys, API and network recovery, links, publishing metadata, visual baselines, performance, accessibility, security policy, and aggregate Cookie/Web Storage privacy budgets. It writes bilingual human reports plus machine-readable JSON, SARIF, JUnit, repair plans, policy reviews, issue drafts, manifests, verification evidence, and freshness-aware GO/REVIEW/NO-GO release decisions.

RealityCheck never treats an unsupported check as passed. Audit mode is read-only, remote targets require explicit authorization, and generated GitHub issue drafts are local files that are never submitted automatically.

## Quick start: three paths

1. Check online: open the zero-upload checker and choose the original HTML export ZIP, one HTML file, or a note folder. A bounded ZIP32 STORE/DEFLATE archive is verified and extracted locally without execution or upload. Unsafe, sensitive, encrypted, ZIP64, conflicting, damaged, special-file, hidden-record, or oversized input fails closed as a whole.

2. Repair in Codex without cloning: ask `Use $skill-installer to install RealityCheck from https://github.com/KevinwithPanda/RealityHTMLCheck/tree/v0.13.0/realitycheck. If the skill already exists, inspect its pinned version first. If it is v0.13.0, change nothing. If it is older, move it—do not delete it—to a timestamped realitycheck backup outside the skills directory, then install v0.13.0. Stop and report instead of overwriting if a safe backup cannot be made. Tell me the installed version; the Skill will be available on my next turn.` On the next turn attach the export and ask `Use $realitycheck to check and repair the HTML note or export folder I attach. Do not overwrite the originals. Return the before technical report, the repaired working copy, the after report, and every detected unresolved decision. Label the copy directly usable only if the after verification meets the Skill's delivery gate.`

3. Publish and prove: run `npx --yes --package="github:KevinwithPanda/RealityHTMLCheck#v0.13.0" realityhtmlcheck publish ./my-notes --language en`. Only completed exact-final-ZIP Chromium gates receive the publish filename. Deploy only materialized verified bytes, then run `realityhtmlcheck verify-deploy <publish-run> <https-base-url/> --allow-remote` for a point-in-time LIVE MATCH, TRANSFORMED REVIEW, BROKEN, or UNVERIFIED receipt. The permission-separated verified Pages workflow performs this sequence in three jobs.

The online checker may apply only doctype, document-language, and early UTF-8 metadata repairs. Its output is a verified safe-metadata working copy, not a fully repaired or publish-ready claim. Evidence keeps source archive, extracted-content, analysis-candidate, and output identities separate; repeat checks preserve new, resolved, worsened, persistent, and unverified states. Use `npx --yes --package="github:KevinwithPanda/RealityHTMLCheck#v0.13.0" realityhtmlcheck note ./my-notes --language en` for a browser-free local check. Add `--fix-safe` only for those three conservative metadata repairs, `--exclude-html "archive/**"` only for reviewed archive scope, or `--baseline <prior-report.json>` for regression-only comparison.

For recurring exports, the Composite Action with `kind: publish` uploads only its parser-validated exact run and never deploys. The verified Pages workflow stores complete publish evidence plus 30-day live evidence with two provenance-labelled diagnostic screenshots. `diagnostic-with-capsule-fallback` means an incomplete live scenario used local verified-capsule replay bytes; it is not a fully live-response-only render. RealityCheck never uploads from the local checker/CLI, takes cloud-account control, or turns incomplete coverage into a pass.

For an authorized running Web application, use the installed Skill: ask `Use $realitycheck to preview the effective audit policy without opening a browser`, or `Use $realitycheck to audit this authorized local app. Do not modify source.` This advanced mode covers browser stress, accessibility, performance, network, security, privacy, and release-governance evidence.
